author: SupportLoopSurvivor
title: Systemic Moderation Failure
content:
After repeated attacks were expressly tied to demands for public and private apologies, leadership resignations, and the removal of specific players, I reported the conduct as harassment, abuse, targeted retaliation, and coercion. Report included indexed screenshots documenting the incidents, related messages, and the game rules implicated by the conduct concerning harassment and threats being used as leverage to compel players to meet personal demands or continue to be targeted and harassed, going so far as to persist in creating a negative and unenjoyable environment for all players within the server. 

Support confirm receiving the evidence but does not address the reported messages, identify what had been reviewed, or explain whether the conduct was evaluated under its own Terms of Service. Instead, support focuses on coordinated attacks being normal gameplay and redirected individual incidents to the same in-game reporting process, even though the report and supporting evidence had already been submitted. It never addresses the distinction between ordinary PvP and the coercive communications. 

This creates a reporting loop rather than a meaningful resolution. It also raises concerns about whether the process is consistent with Apple’s requirements for handling reports of offensive user-generated content. Published protections offer little value when detailed evidence is acknowledged but its substance remains unaddressed, allowing the reported conduct to continue without any communicated intervention or resolution.

Based on this handling, the only practical option may be to stop playing. However, leaving the game is not a substitute for meaningful enforcement of the protections presented to players. Competitive gameplay does not require accepting harassment, coercive threats, or attacks used to enforce personal demands. The failure to distinguish legitimate competition from conduct prohibited by the game’s own published rules has made this an extremely negative environment and experience.

author: GunchGunch
title: One Year Later–
content:
Started playing this game as a boredom-killer, and I made a goal for myself: Play for a year and come up with an actual review. I got a lot to say, but this will be 100% honest, so here we go!

First Impressions: This is most definitely one of those social mobile games where progress is pretty quick in the beginning, and eventually it’ll slow, and you’re gonna have to be seeking the help of others w the social aspect of the game: alliances.
I lucked out with my alliances I chose, I’ve been through 3. Most people in this game are very friendly and helpful! I definitely have a great time in an active, engaged alliance, and it does feel good to partake in alliances that perform well!
I will say: There are a handful of unspoken rules that I did have to learn the hard way, mainly regarding server etiquette that seems to be specific to this game (Namely– the plundering etiquette. Just a bit of a learning curve early-on for most players, it seems, as some people can be very unforgiving about it).
I am f2p, as top-up prices are among the most inflated I’ve ever seen for any mobile game, but honestly the game is pretty generous! I have yet to feel like I’ve had to spend a dedicated amount of time on resource -gathering, something that has really killed my interest in mobile games in the past.

Also, yes: if you want to be playing the zombie levels shown in the ads, they’re mostly in the beginning of the game during early growth. Good luck with Frontline Breakthrough to continue that gameplay though, many of the levels are near-impossible and the YouTube “Tutorials” they provide are not accurate to the actual game (Diff speed for dmg-dealing, diff amounts of enemies, just average mobile game misrepresentation of their game, I guess it can’t be helped. Not like this game mode does much for your overall performance anyways, but I Would, in fact, call this practice pretty Scummy.)

I Guess this comes with most online games, but the world chat is pretty bad– lots of nsfw talking points, and it seems that the support for the reporting system seems to be kinda spotty. Some of these mfs are taking this game way too damn seriously, but I guess that type of crowd can come with any online game. Just be warned, the moderation seems to be pretty 50/50 as to whether or not they want to actually moderate (or, it’s simply AI that can’t moderate). The game should probably be rated 18+ for the world chat alone, I ended up just blocking a handful of individuals that were just blatantly crudely nsfw, publicly malicious about other players, flaunting bigotry (slurs will always find a way, ig? lol), and/or just plain obnoxious; this might be the best solution for most. I was just tired of seeing it constantly on the bottom of my screen.

Other than that, being a social butterfly in this game definitely has its perks: As a low-level player, I found I grew the most when I was just participating– yeah I wouldn’t be doing as much damage as my teammates, but every alliance I was in simply counted on an active effort and participation. I definitely wasn’t pulling any weight early-on, but everyone was always extremely kind and simply valued the people that Showed Up and Tried for events, regardless of your numbers! Most alliances are definitely more positive about growth, and it really inspired me to grow more over time!

And finally: would I recommend this game? Sure, why not! If you’re into the idea of slowly growing a base and making lots of great connections via the social aspect, you’ll definitely have a lot of fun! No, the ads aren’t wholly representative of the game beyond a single, mostly insignificant gamemode. The competitive scene isn’t for me, I find the culture there annoying, personally. After a year playing, I won’t be uninstalling, and I do enjoy doing my dailies and checking on my base throughout the day! Overall, a solid 3.5/5, but I’ll round up for the sake of this review.

author: Paulosilva123
title: Player Warning
content:
⚠️ Player Warning – Read Before Spending Money on “Last War”

This is a warning based on my personal experience with the mobile game Last War.

I spent over $470 USD on in-app purchases believing I was playing a fair free-to-play strategy game. After questioning gameplay balance and alliance dynamics in public chat, I was removed from my alliance and became the target of continuous harassment and intimidation from stronger players.

I received messages saying my account would be “hunted forever,” used as a “piggy bank for resources,” and that I would only be “safe” if I joined a specific alliance. The environment became hostile and unplayable.

I reported this to the game’s support system. No action was taken.
Eventually, I had to delete my character just to escape the harassment — and discovered that all paid progress was permanently lost, meaning I would have to spend money again to reach the same level.

I’m sharing this so others understand the risks:
	•	There is no meaningful protection for paying players
	•	Harassment and economic pressure are tolerated
	•	In-app purchases can lose all value instantly
	•	Questioning the system can make you a target

Spend carefully. Document everything. And don’t assume money spent equals safety or fairness.

This is not a rant — it’s a consumer warning.

title: Paying money is the only skill you’ll need for the game
content:

It becomes an idle game. I will praise the game for 0 ads. It becomes a series of micro transactions. I played for free, I became strangely addicted and liked the challenge of paying no money. I soon realized I wasn’t playing a game. I was just clicking on buttons with no strategy or skill. 

I joined an alliance of about 80 people. You can compete against other alliances every week.  For a small example you can complete a task every 4 hours for points towards the competition. Alternatively you can spend 3 bucks here and there to complete tasks more frequently to boost your points in the competition.

If you came here because of the cool ads, you’ll  have more fun playing sodoku. If you like idle games and have a strange spending addiction then this game is up your alley.

author: Pribnuts82
title: Deceptive Advertising, Bait and Switch gameplay, money grabbing
content:
See title.  It’s a scam like all other games being advertised like this.  Even the screenshots in the App Store are from the ads — NOT the game.  The first couple of hours has some gameplay that “looks” like the ads but has no bearing on the game mechanics. your time is spent upgrading a base and waiting to level up to actually play (you can always pay real money not to wait).  At level 12 or so the game completely shifts away from their ad style to a PvP environment where you have to join an alliance to move forward, and forced to play/“win” micro battles to earn miniscule resources you have to accrue over days and weeks to level up (unless you pay real money of course).  The game is top heavy with whales decimating anyone below them.  The only way to compete is to pay a LOT of money. Initial level-to-reward payout is free, enabling rapid level advancement with the intent of hooking you with Pavlovian-inspired “cha-ching” and “hoorah” sounds.  Eventually, around level 13 or so the resource rewards are minimal and leveling up takes days to weeks - unless you pay of course.

It’s repetitive pyramid scheme style gameplay, where you need to exponentially spend resources (or real money) a e.g., 1 item to upgrade to the next level, and then two of that item,  then 4, then 8, etc.  All mechanics work like this - component parts, hero leveling, base leveling, time to upgrade…doubling resource gathering but quadrupling the resource cost at each level, etc.  again, you can reduce this time with real money - and not a minimal amount.  

The devs are obviously looking for whales to fund the scheme.

I suggest the FTC be involved.

author: Golddesk53
title: Terrible
content:
I’ve played this game for a long time and have invested a significant amount of time and effort into helping grow my server. Unfortunately, the competitive balance system has made it clear that some servers simply are not given a realistic chance to succeed.

Server 165 has consistently struggled to compete for first place, and despite repeated feedback from many players, the response has essentially been, “We understand your frustration, but we can’t promise any changes.”

The biggest issue is that the current transfer system creates a cycle where struggling servers cannot recruit the players they need to improve, which means they continue struggling indefinitely. Players are expected to keep spending time and money while knowing they have little chance of ever competing at the highest level.

Customer support has been polite and responsive, but acknowledging a problem without taking action does not solve anything. A competitive game should provide every active server with a realistic path to improve and win. Right now, that does not feel like the case.

Unless the developers make meaningful changes to server balancing and transfer seat allocation, many dedicated players will continue to lose motivation and leave the game.

author: Surface Citizen
title: A $3000 Lesson in Disappointment
content:
I’ve played Last War for about a year and spent several thousand dollars on it, and I have to give it only one star.

The truth is, most of the joy comes from your teammates — those wonderful, kind people you meet along the way. But the game itself offers little in terms of actual gameplay. Most of it is repetitive and exhausting, and even if you spend thousands of dollars, you might still just be an average player.

The way the game is designed, unless you are in the No.1 alliance with multiple “big whales,” those who spent half a million. You’re always at risk of losing your friends. Whales tend to band together, and other members usually follow them. That means if you want to keep enjoying the game, you’re forced to constantly hop from one alliance to another, always chasing bigger whales.

This cycle leads to endless separations, endless people quitting, and it’s incredibly painful. One moment, you’re fighting side by side with your friends; the next moment, they’re recruited away by a bigger whale. That’s not fun, and honestly, that’s not what a game should be.

author: Thegr8bambino86

author: WasFunAtFirst
title: Was fun in the beginning
content: Last War is a fun game to play in the beginning when you are challenged to build a fortress and fight zombies… but that changes quickly to be about being part of an alliance and then plundering and fighting other players and other alliances.  It quickly turns from fun to outright frustrating especially since you are still fairly low in progressing & power — and keep getting trashed by other higher ranked/powered players.  Soon became as frustrating as real life so was time to delete my character, account and remove the game.  Need t go find something else fun and less stressful.

author: xMiK117

author: CleverNameIGuess

author: Zelderian
title: Incredibly misleading- no surprise there
content:
The ads you see make up the first few minutes of gameplay, and then they introduce the typical real-time base building that is actually the game. The minigames you see from the ads are just a small part of the game, and they try to sell you on a ton of fluff gameplay that doesn’t matter.

author: Adrian5201
title: False advertisement (A MUST READ: Be Careful)
content: This is my first review of a game and application. I’m generally easygoing and not much bothers me. When I clicked the link and downloaded the app, expecting to play the game I saw advertised, the actual game was nothing like what was shown. author: JetDL

author: Magnustampa

author: Gotbidnezz
title: Misogyny is Alive and Well here
content:
I am a woman who has enjoyed this game. As other reviews have explained, it becomes more involved after the stage advertised. You eventually join an alliance of other players and strategize as a team. The actual game I would give a high rating. I will explain below why my rating is low. 

There was a man who joined our alliance who, as we later discovered, had been kicked out of other alliances for threatening, bullying, and misogynistic behavior. He exhibited the same behavior in our alliance and was kicked out. He created an entirely false narrative that I led a racist campaign against him and other players which led to his removal from our alliance. 

He has used this as an excuse to harass me for months. This includes obvious threats, demeaning comments, repeated unwanted communications, and other disturbing behavior. When reported, I am repeatedly told that his behavior does not violate any guidelines. 

Because the game deveIopers will do nothing about this, I began posting screenshots of his messages and behavior on my public profile to warn other players. Then, the developers give me warnings about malicious speech and remove the posts when all I have done is post the same messages and behavior that I have been told is acceptable. He has stated the only way he will stop harassing me is if I comply with his orders and demands and that these screenshots are the justification for his behavior. But that is untrue, because he has repeatedly asks my teammates where I am because he can’t find me only so he can harass me again, so whether the screenshots are posted has nothing to do with his behavior. 

While my team, and especially the men on it, have been very supportive, it’s distressing that the developers and administrators of the game continue to allow this to happen to the women who play this game. Women be warned.

author: Superpresto
title: Repetitive, Boring, and Somehow Overrated
content:
I gave Last War a shot after seeing the endless ads, and I’ll admit — it is exactly what the ads show. But let’s be honest: just because a game is accurately advertised doesn’t mean it deserves a 5-star rating. If this is what passes for top-tier mobile gaming now, we’re either in trouble or collectively losing our taste.

The gameplay gets old fast. You do the same thing over and over with minimal challenge, no real variety, and hardly any strategy. It feels more like a time-killer than a game you actually look forward to playing. Two stars for functioning and being what it says it is — but fun? Not really.

author: Rabidpuffin
title: A lot of fun until…
content: A lot of fun until you run up against the inevitable speed bumps of time. It’s not long into playing that buildings take 10+ hours to upgrade unless you buy packs with real money.
